newsitem.title: USA: Earthgrains sees charge for plant closing.
newsitem.headline: Earthgrains sees charge for plant closing.

text.p: Earthgrains Co said Monday it expects to take a one-time, after-tax charge of $6.0 million to $8.0 million in the fiscal fourth quarter related to the planned closure of a refrigerated dough plant in Indianapolis.
Earthgrains said it decided to close the Indianapolis plant by the end of March and transfer production to its plant in Carrollton, Texas.
The production transfer will not affect refrigerated dough revenues and is expected to generate cost savings, the company said.
The company did not say how many employees would be affected by the move. Earthgrains officials were not immediately available for comment.

Earthgrains also said its board of directors approved a proposal to build a bakery in northern Portgual to meet increasing demand for baked goods in that country and western Spain. The bakery is expected to be operational in the summer of 1998.

"Additional capacity in Portugal will allow us to continue increasing market share in Portugal and further bolster our market-leading position in Spain for Bimbo brand fresh baked goods," Barry Beracha, chairman and chief executive officer, said in a statement. "European baking is an important part of the Earthgrains Co. We plan to continue investing in this growing business."
Earthgrains is the third-largest producer of baked good and the second-largest maker of refrigerated dough in the United States.
